title: Why Basie had him play in a cup mute
summary: Basie wanted him in a mute only on record sessions; on the road he played the same solos open in big warehouses.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: : Now, just going back to Basie, how do you come to get sort of rather typed with the cup mute?

Oh, because Basie always asked me to play in a mute. I don't know why. Because after we made the record, I could play the same solo that night open because he can't play in those big, those big tobacco warehouses down in North Carolina in the mute.
So, but only at the record session he'd ask me to play it in the mute. And then when I get down there, I could play it in any way I wanted to.
Play the same solo open that I recorded with a mute.
